name: Nilüfer Yanya
label: Ninja Tune
lede: A Chelsea kid with a saz-playing father, three EPs and an Adele support slot, then the album Pitchfork filed at No. 13 for 2024.

eras.title: A saz at home, a Saturday school down the road
eras.text: A Chelsea childhood between a painter father's Ottoman records and a Saturday music school, then a SoundCloud page and an offer she turned down.

years.h: Born in London to two visual artists
years.p: Yanya grows up in Chelsea with a Turkish father and an Irish-Barbadian mother, both artists, and starts guitar at 12.
years.xp:
According to Tone Glow, her father played the saz and Ottoman classical music at home while her mother took her to museums and galleries. She practiced piano daily and wrote songs on guitar through her teens.

At Saturday music school a songwriting teacher told her, in her recollection: "Your songs are really cool, you could really do this if you want."

years.h: Demos go up on SoundCloud, and a girl group offer goes nowhere
years.p: Yanya posts her first songs online in 2014, then turns down a spot in a girl group produced by One Direction's Louis Tomlinson.
years.xp: Wikipedia records her verdict on the pitch: "Let's go and pinch some young people, tell them we're going to make a really successful group." She kept writing alone instead.

eras.title: Small crimes, three EPs
eras.text: First gigs, then three EPs in three years, enough to get an American label's attention before she had an album.

years.h: She emails a promoter and plays Troubadour in Earl's Court
years.p: Her first solo show comes from a cold email to the booking promoter at the Troubadour; she then plays solo often from about age 21 before adding a band.

years.h: Small Crimes / Keep on Calling, the first EP
years.p: Her debut EP arrives in 2016, the start of a run of EPs before any album.

years.h: Plant Feed EP
years.p: The second EP in as many years, recorded while she was still playing small rooms around London.

years.src: The Fader: Watch Nilüfer Yanya's poised Tiny Desk Concert
years.h: Do You Like Pain?, with "Baby Luv" on it
years.p: The third EP carries "Baby Luv", which she still plays a year later at NPR's Tiny Desk.

eras.title: Miss Universe and a locked-down year
eras.text: The debut album lands on ATO, the touring stops, and she plays NPR's Tiny Desk from home.

years.h: Miss Universe: seventeen tracks, eight producers
years.p: The debut album runs 52 minutes and is stitched with voicemail-style interludes credited to "WWAY Health", a parody wellness company.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, sessions ran from January 2016 to October 2018 at Press Play and Grow in London, Riverfish in Penzance and studios in Los Angeles. The producers include [[Wilma Archer|461dbdf1-bfc7-4e6e-a165-2b2d678ceb8a]], [[John Congleton|6da4067f-e6ce-49b6-925c-56e017075038]], [[Dave Okumu|abb29383-f013-479d-bf75-1cd57c9b95ed]] and Lucy Lu.

Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and later put it in its 50 best albums of 2019. Metacritic scores it 85.

years.src: The Fader: Watch Nilüfer Yanya's poised Tiny Desk Concert
years.h: Tiny Desk, with a saxophone and three songs
years.p: She plays "Baby Luv", "The Unordained" and "Angels" for NPR with Jazzi Bobbi on sax, Lucy Lu on bass and Ellis Dupuy on drums.

years.src: NME: Nilüfer Yanya debuts new track, Day 7 · XPN: Watch Nilüfer Yanya play a Tiny Desk Concert at home in London
years.h: Tiny Desk (Home) debuts "Day 7"
years.p: With venues shut, she plays NPR's Tiny Desk from home in London and premieres the new song "Day 7".

years.h: Feeling Lucky? EP, led by "Crash"
years.p: A short EP between albums, with a video for "Crash".

years.h: "Stabilise" is the first sign of Painless
years.p: The single arrives two months after the Inside Out compilation of her first three EPs.

eras.title: Painless, Hyde Park and a long tour
eras.text: Album two lands in the year-end lists and puts her in front of the biggest crowds she has played.

years.src: Wikipedia: Painless (album) · NPR Music via KLCC: On Painless, Nilüfer Yanya doesn't play nice · Consequence: Nilüfer Yanya on her whirlwind, rewarding 2022
years.h: Painless: Pitchfork 8.4 and a Best New Music tag
years.p: Producers are Will Archer, Jazzi Bobbi, Bullion and Andrew Sarlo, and it peaks at No. 86 on the UK chart.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Laura Snapes wrote that it "excels at a kind of subtle disclosure", leaning on texture over power. The album landed at No. 16 on Pitchfork's 2022 list, No. 30 on NPR's and No. 10 at Consequence.

NPR noted she was tired of being called R&B: "It's definitely rock music." Four singles ran ahead of it: "Stabilise", "Midnight Sun", "Anotherlife" and "The Dealer".

years.src: Wikipedia: Nilüfer Yanya · Consequence: Nilüfer Yanya on her whirlwind, rewarding 2022
years.h: She opens for Adele at Hyde Park
years.p: Adele's first UK shows in five years get Yanya on the bill, and she also opens the UK arena dates of Roxy Music's 50th anniversary tour.
years.xp: Consequence counted eight straight months of touring by late November across North America, the UK and Europe, including Coachella and a May show at Webster Hall in New York. She called Webster Hall "such a moment"; her drummer tested positive for COVID afterward.

years.h: She sings on Bombay Bicycle Club's "Meditate"
years.p: The guest spot is on My Big Day by [[Bombay Bicycle Club|0ae49abe-d6af-44fa-8ab0-b9ace5690e6f]].

years.src: God Is in the TV: Nilüfer Yanya, My Method Actor · Alt Press interview: Nilüfer Yanya, how memory and emotion built My Method Actor · Wikipedia: Wilma Archer
years.h: Yanya and Will Archer disappear to Wales and Eastbourne
years.p: God Is in the TV dates the sessions for her next album to early 2023 in London, Wales and Eastbourne.
years.xp: The plan, she told Alt Press: "we were going to work on it, just us two, and not really share anything until we had to." Archer, also known as Wilma Archer, had worked on her records since Miss Universe.

eras.title: Method acting, Ninja Tune and Lorde's arenas
eras.text: A new label, one producer, and a third album that puts her on Pitchfork's year-end list.

years.src: Alt Press video: Nilüfer Yanya plays a hesitant bride
years.h: "Like I Say (I Runaway)" ends a two-year silence
years.p: Her sister Molly Daniel directs the video, with Yanya as a bride who bolts into the woods.
years.xp: Alt Press quotes her on the idea: "It's about how you choose to spend your time. Time is like a currency." The track pairs '90s college-radio fuzz with Archer's production.

years.src: Wikipedia: My Method Actor · Stereogum: Nilüfer Yanya's infinite melodies · Alt Press interview: Nilüfer Yanya, how memory and emotion built My Method Actor · Under the Radar: My Method Actor review
years.h: My Method Actor: Pitchfork 8.5, No. 13 of 2024
years.p: Her first album for Ninja Tune is produced by Will Archer alone; Pitchfork's 8.5 review calls it "an album that has the feel of everyday luxury".
years.xp:
Stereogum reports it is the first album where she worked with one producer rather than several; she says the old way came from insecurity. Archer, who has also produced for Jessie Ware and Sudan Archives, handled the music while she wrote.

Metacritic scores it 85. It topped the UK Independent Albums chart and reached No. 53 on the main UK chart. Year-end: Exclaim! No. 14, Uncut No. 55, Under the Radar No. 2. Singles were "Like I Say (I Runaway)", "Method Actor", "Call It Love" and "Mutations".

years.big: "the way I write songs, and perform, is like method acting"
years.src: Alt Press interview: Nilüfer Yanya, how memory and emotion built My Method Actor
years.h: Where the title came from
years.p: She tells Alt Press the phrase was already a lyric before it became the album's name.
years.xp: The Gibson SG runs through the record, alongside recorded strings and what she calls an "unusual electronic thing", both new for her.

years.h: Lorde picks her for the Ultrasound World Tour
years.p: She is announced as a supporting act, taking her into arenas again after Hyde Park.

years.h: Dancing Shoes EP
years.p: A short follow-up EP to My Method Actor, also on Ninja Tune.
